questions.q: How does a dashboard filter differ from a report filter?
options: A dashboard filter permanently edits the source report
A dashboard filter is chosen by the viewer at view time and narrows widgets without editing the reports
A dashboard filter only works on tabular reports
There is no difference
questions.explain: Report filters are baked into the report. Dashboard filters are viewer-chosen and layer on top of each widget's own report filters.

questions.q: A dashboard filter on Account Name seems to have no effect on one widget. What is the most likely cause?
options: The widget is a metric
Dashboards can only filter one widget at a time
The widget's source report does not include Account Name, so the filter cannot match it
The filter must be re-created every day
questions.explain: A widget responds only if its source report has the filtered field, typically through its report type.

questions.q: In SOQL terms, what does a dashboard filter behave like?
options: A GROUP BY clause
An extra WHERE condition added on top of the report's own filters
A LIMIT clause
An ORDER BY clause
questions.explain: The report filters still apply, and the dashboard filter adds another condition.

questions.q: Which is true about the number of filters on a Lightning dashboard, per this lesson?
options: Unlimited, as many as you like
Only one is ever allowed
Only a small number is allowed, commonly three
Filters are only allowed on text widgets
questions.explain: Lightning dashboards cap the number of filters, commonly at three, so pick fields that matter to every viewer.

questions.q: Which button in the toolbar starts a new dashboard filter?
options: + Filter
Done
Save As
View Report
questions.explain: The + Filter button, next to + Widget, opens the dashboard filter builder.
